findings.description: Long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded directly in the Lambda environment variables in the Terraform source. These are stored in state, visible to anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, and committed to version control, allowing credential theft and lateral movement.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the Lambda environment variables (which contain secrets here) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are returned in plaintext to any principal able to read the function configuration, with no separate KMS key policy boundary.
The function uses nodejs12.x, a runtime that has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unaddressed.

The function has no vpc_config, so it runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network segmentation controls, easing data exfiltration if the function is compromised.
